This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	# 构建与链接：build.rs 如何找到藏在 extras 里的 CUPTI
2	
3	> **承接上一讲（u1-l1）**：你已经知道 pegainfer-cupti 是 Rust 通向 NVIDIA CUPTI Range Profiler 的一座桥，四个文件分工明确，唯一公开 API 是 `profile_range_with_prepare`。本讲回答下一个自然的问题：**那份约 400 行的 C++ 实现（`csrc/range_profiler.cpp`）是怎么被编译成库、CUPTI 的头文件和库又是怎么被找到并链接进来的？** 全部答案集中在 crate 里那份只有 34 行的 `build.rs`。
4	
5	## 1. 本讲目标
6	
7	学完本讲，你应该能够：
8	
9	1. 说清 `build.rs` 在 Cargo 构建流程中的位置——它在包被编译之前运行，通过 `println!("cargo:...")` 向 Cargo 回传指令，影响后续的编译与链接。

16	
17	### 2.1 build.rs：Cargo 的构建脚本
18	
19	`build.rs` 是 Cargo 约定的特殊文件：如果你的包根目录下有它，Cargo 会**先把它编译成可执行文件并运行**，然后才开始编译你的包。它通常用来：
20	
21	- 生成 Rust 代码或头文件；
22	- 编译宿主机的 C/C++ 代码；
23	- 探测外部依赖（比如 CUDA 工具链）的位置。
24	
25	构建脚本通过标准输出向 Cargo「回话」：所有以 `cargo:` 开头的行都是指令，其余行只是普通日志。本讲会见到三种指令：
26	
27	| 指令 | 作用 |
28	|---|---|
29	| `cargo:rustc-link-search=native=<路径>` | 告诉 rustc：链接时把这个路径加入库搜索路径（相当于给最终链接加一个 `-L`） |
30	| `cargo:rustc-link-lib=<名字>` | 告诉 rustc：最终链接时链接名为 `<名字>` 的库（相当于 `-l`） |
31	| `cargo:rerun-if-changed=<路径>` | 告诉 Cargo：只有这个路径变化时才重新运行构建脚本 |
32	
33	一个关键心智模型：**这些指令不是立刻生效的**。它们被 Cargo 收集起来，在「最终把整个 crate（以及依赖它的二进制）链接成产物」的那一步才变成 `-L` / `-l` 参数。
34	
35	### 2.2 编译与链接：两条搜索路径
36	
37	C/C++ 构建要过两关，每关都有自己的搜索路径：
38	
39	- **编译关（头文件）**：`#include <cupti.h>` 能否找到，取决于 `-I` 指定的头文件搜索路径（以及编译器的默认路径）。
40	- **链接关（库文件）**：`-lcupti` 要在 `-L` 指定的库搜索路径里找到 `libcupti.so` 或 `libcupti.a`（以及系统默认路径）。
41	
42	pegainfer-cupti 的设计哲学是**错误前置**：CUDA/CUPTI 缺失时，让构建在编译期或链接期就失败，而不是把问题拖到运行期。三个阶段对应的失败形式：
43	
44	| 阶段 | 缺什么 | 典型报错（示意） |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| 编译期 | 找不到 CUPTI 头文件 | `fatal error: cupti_profiler_target.h: No such file or directory` |
47	| 链接期 | 找不到 `libcupti` | `cannot find -lcupti` |
48	| 运行期 | （本项目设计上不允许漏到这里） | —— |
49	
50	### 2.3 cc crate：build-dependency 里的常客
51	
52	[cc](https://crates.io/crates/cc) 是 Rust 生态里最常用的构建依赖之一：它把「找到系统 C/C++ 编译器、拼参数、调用」包装成了声明式的 `cc::Build` API。本讲的 `build.rs` 用它把一份 C++ 源文件编成**静态库**。特别注意 `compile(name)` 这一步会自动做两件事：
53	
54	1. 调用 C++ 编译器把所有 `.file(...)` 登记的源文件编成 `lib<name>.a`；
55	2. 自动向 Cargo 发出 `cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=<name>` 与指向产物目录的 `cargo:rustc-link-search` 指令。
56	
57	也就是说，cc 负责「我自己编出来的库」的链接声明；**外部系统库**（CUDA、CUPTI、libstdc++）则要 build.rs 自己用 `cargo:rustc-link-lib` 声明——这是 4.3 节的主角。
58	
59	### 2.4 CUPTI 是什么、装在哪
60	
61	CUPTI（CUDA Profiling Tools Interface）是 NVIDIA 官方的性能分析接口层：读硬件性能计数器、做 kernel 时间线插桩都靠它。它与 nvcc、cuBLAS 这类「跑程序」的组件不同，属于「观测程序」的组件。因此在经典的 CUDA 安装中，它不在主 `include/`、`lib64/` 里，而在：
62	
63	```
64	<CUDA 根目录>/extras/CUPTI/include   ← 头文件（如 cupti.h、cupti_profiler_target.h）
65	<CUDA 根目录>/extras/CUPTI/lib64     ← 库文件（libcupti.so）
66	```
67	
68	`build.rs` 第 6 行的注释说的就是这件事，原文是：`// CUPTI ships outside the main toolkit dirs in classic installs.`（CUPTI 在经典安装中不随主工具链目录发布。）另外，各发行版也可能通过包管理器单独安装 CUPTI（装进系统头文件/库目录），所以探测逻辑必须容忍「extras 下没有」的情况——这正是 4.2 节 `is_dir()` 分支存在的原因。
69

98	### 4.1 CudaToolkit::discover 与 root/include_dirs：先回答「CUDA 装在哪」
99	
100	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
101	
102	任何想引用 CUDA 头文件的原生代码构建，都要先回答同一个问题：**这台机器的 CUDA 工具链根目录在哪？** 答案并不唯一——可能是 `/usr/local/cuda` 软链接，可能是 `/usr/local/cuda-12.4`，可能是包管理器装的散件，也可能只存在于某个自定义前缀里；`nvcc` 可能在 `PATH` 里也可能不在。
103	
104	openinfer workspace 的做法是把「找 CUDA」这件事抽成一个共享 crate：`pegainfer-build`，对外提供 `CudaToolkit` 类型。这样「CUDA 在哪」在整个仓库里只有一份答案，修一处、处处生效——这就是「单一事实来源」在构建系统里的体现（u1-l1 的实践已经让你用 `grep -rn "pegainfer-cupti" --include=Cargo.toml` 看过谁在引用谁；对 `pegainfer-build` 可以用同样的办法列出它的消费方）。

107	
108	从 build.rs 的视角，探测与消费只有五步：
109	
110	```

112	    │
113	    ▼
114	CudaToolkit::discover()            # 定位 CUDA 工具链，返回 toolkit
115	    │
116	    ├─ toolkit.root                # 工具链根目录（PathBuf），4.2 节用它拼 extras 路径
117	    ├─ toolkit.include_dirs        # 主工具链头文件目录集合 → 4.3 节喂给 cc
118	    └─ toolkit.link_search()       # 发出主工具链的 cargo:rustc-link-search 指令
119	```

122

195	### 4.2 CUPTI 头文件与 lib64 的 extras 路径处理
196	
197	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
198	
199	经典安装的 CUDA 工具链目录大致长这样（**示意图**，具体条目随 CUDA 版本与安装形态变化）：
200	
201	```
202	/usr/local/cuda/                 ← toolkit.root 指向这里
203	├── bin/                         ← nvcc 等
204	├── include/                     ← cuda.h、cublas_v2.h 等主头文件
205	├── lib64/                       ← 主库
206	└── extras/
207	    └── CUPTI/
208	        ├── include/             ← CUPTI 头文件
209	        └── lib64/               ← libcupti
210	```
211	
212	CUPTI 被放在 `extras/` 下，是因为它**不参与程序的编译与运行**，只在「分析程序」时才需要——工具链把「跑起来必需」与「观测用」分开放。这带来一个构建上的麻烦：光知道 `toolkit.root` 还不够，还得知道 CUPTI 另有藏身处；而且**不是所有安装都有这个目录**（最小安装，或发行版把 CUPTI 单独装进系统目录的形态）。所以 build.rs 的策略是：extras 路径「**存在才追加，不存在就交给系统默认搜索路径**」。
213	
214	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
215	
216	```
217	cupti_include = root + "extras/CUPTI/include"
218	cupti_lib64   = root + "extras/CUPTI/lib64"
219	
220	编译配置阶段：
221	    if cupti_include.is_dir()  → cc 追加这条 -I                    （L17-L19）
222	链接指令阶段：
223	    if cupti_lib64.is_dir()    → 发出 cargo:rustc-link-search=...   （L23-L25）
224	
225	两个 if 都不命中（CUPTI 不在 extras）：
226	    → 不追加任何东西，编译器/链接器回落到系统默认搜索路径
227	    → 系统里装了 CUPTI（如包管理器形态）→ 一切正常
228	    → 系统里根本没有 CUPTI → 编译期（找不到头文件）或链接期（找不到库）失败
229	```
230	
231	注意最后一点：**失败被明确地留在构建期**。这是有意设计——一个引用了 CUPTI 符号的二进制如果到运行时才发现缺库，排查成本高得多。
232	
233	#### 4.2.3 源码精读
234	
235	两个路径的定义已在 4.1.3 引用过（L7-L8）；这里看两处「条件追加」：
236	
237	> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L17-L19](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L17-L19)
238	> 编译配置阶段：只有当 extras 下的 CUPTI include 目录真实存在时，才把它追加进 cc 的头文件搜索路径。
239	
240	```rust
241	if cupti_include.is_dir() {
242	    build.include(&cupti_include);
243	}
244	```
245	
246	> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L23-L25](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L23-L25)
247	> 链接指令阶段：同理，只有 extras 下的 CUPTI lib64 真实存在时，才向 Cargo 发出对应的库搜索路径指令。
248	
249	```rust
250	if cupti_lib64.is_dir() {
251	    println!("cargo:rustc-link-search=native={}", cupti_lib64.display());
252	}
253	```
254

295	### 4.3 cc 编译与链接指令输出：从一份 .cpp 到一张链接清单
296	
297	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
298	
299	`cc::Build` 是「编译作业的声明式描述」：先链式登记属性，最后一次 `compile()` 收尾。收尾时它做两件事——把登记的源文件编成**静态库**，并自动发出链接这个静态库所需的 cargo 指令（见 2.3 节）。但 cc 只管「自己编的东西」；**外部系统库**（cuda、cupti、stdc++）必须由 build.rs 自己用 `cargo:rustc-link-lib` 一条条声明。本模块把这两段拼成一张完整的「链接清单」。
300	
301	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
302	
303	build.rs 的 `main` 一共四段，一气呵成：
304	
305	```
306	① 探测准备   L4-L8    manifest_dir、toolkit、两个 extras 路径（4.1/4.2 已讲）
307	② cc 编译    L10-L20  配置并编译 range_profiler.cpp → libpegainfer_cupti_range_profiler.a
308	③ 链接指令   L22-L31  主 -L、extras -L、三条 -l
309	④ 增量声明   L33      rerun-if-changed
310	```
311	
312	最终 rustc 在链接时收到的库相关参数（**示意**，实际拼写以你机器上 `-v` 输出为准）：
313	
314	```
315	-L <主工具链 lib64>                  ← toolkit.link_search()（L22）
316	-L <extras/CUPTI/lib64>              ← L24，存在时
317	-l pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler    ← cc 自动发出（静态库本体）
318	-l cuda                              ← L27
319	-l cupti                             ← L28
320	-l stdc++                            ← L30，非 Windows
321	```

324	
325	cc 配置链：
326	
327	> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L10-L20](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L10-L20)
328	> 用 cc 把 `csrc/range_profiler.cpp` 编成静态库：开 C++ 模式、锁 C++17、关警告、登记唯一的源文件、并入主工具链头文件路径，最后在 L20 收尾。

330	```rust
331	let mut build = cc::Build::new();
332	build
333	    .cpp(true)
334	    .std("c++17")
335	    .warnings(false)
336	    .file(manifest_dir.join("csrc/range_profiler.cpp"))
337	    .includes(&toolkit.include_dirs);
338	if cupti_include.is_dir() {

344	逐项理由：
345	
346	- `.cpp(true)`：使用 C++ 编译器驱动（g++/clang++），而非 C 编译器。
347	- `.std("c++17")`：实现代码按 C++17 编写，CUPTI 的 profiler 系列头文件与实现用到的语言特性以此为前提。
348	- `.warnings(false)`：相当于向编译器传 `-w`，屏蔽这份自带 C++ 文件的编译警告——它不参与日常 Rust lint 反馈环，警告只会制造噪音。
349	- `.file(...)`：只编译这一个文件——它就是上一讲认识的、约 400 行的 CUPTI 会话实现。
350	- `.includes(&toolkit.include_dirs)` 加上条件追加的 `.include(&cupti_include)`：头文件搜索路径的完整来源（主工具链 + 可能的 CUPTI extras）。
351	- `.compile("pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler")`：产出 `libpegainfer_cupti_range_profiler.a`，并自动发出 `cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler` 与指向产物目录的 `rustc-link-search`。

353	链接指令段：
354	
355	> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L27-L31](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L27-L31)

358	```rust
359	println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=cuda");
360	println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=cupti");
361	if !cfg!(target_os = "windows") {
362	    println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=stdc++");
363	}
364	```
365	
366	- `-lcuda`：实现在 C++ 里直接调用了 CUDA **Driver API**（如上下文获取与同步，详见单元 2/3 的讲义），这些符号在 `libcuda` 里。
367	- `-lcupti`：本 crate 的存在意义——`cuptiProfilerInitialize` 等一系列 profiler 符号都来自它。
368	- `-lstdc++`：C++ 实现用了标准库（异常、字符串等）；非 Windows 平台上最终链接由 rustc 驱动，不会自动带上 C++ 标准库，必须显式声明。Windows/MSVC 走另一套 CRT 链接机制，因此有 `if !cfg!(target_os = "windows")` 分支。
369	
370	增量声明：
371	
372	> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L33](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L33)
373	> 告诉 Cargo：只有这份 C++ 源文件变化时才重新运行构建脚本。
374	
375	```rust
376	println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=csrc/range_profiler.cpp");
377	```
378	
379	语义要点（Cargo 手册规定）：
380	
381	1. 如果一个 build.rs **没有**发出任何 `rerun-if-changed`，Cargo 采用保守策略——包内**任何**文件变化都重跑构建脚本。
382	2. 一旦发出了哪怕一条，保守策略即被关闭，Cargo 只监视列出的路径。
383	3. 构建脚本自身（`build.rs`）的变化永远会触发重跑，这是内建行为，不需要也不能用这条指令表达。
384	
385	对这个 crate 而言，L33 意味着：改 `src/lib.rs`、改文档，都不会重跑 build.rs（自然也不会重编 C++）；只有改 `range_profiler.cpp`（或 `build.rs` 本身）才会。收益是构建更快；代价是：如果未来新增第二个 `.cpp`/`.cu` 文件却忘了同步登记 `rerun-if-changed`，改它不会触发重编——这是使用该指令时最常见的坑。

# 构建与链接：build.rs 如何找到藏在 extras 里的 CUPTI

> **承接上一讲（u1-l1）**：你已经知道 pegainfer-cupti 是 Rust 通向 NVIDIA CUPTI Range Profiler 的一座桥，四个文件分工明确，唯一公开 API 是 `profile_range_with_prepare`。本讲回答下一个自然的问题：**那份约 400 行的 C++ 实现（`csrc/range_profiler.cpp`）是怎么被编译成库、CUPTI 的头文件和库又是怎么被找到并链接进来的？** 全部答案集中在 crate 里那份只有 34 行的 `build.rs`。

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. 说清 `build.rs` 在 Cargo 构建流程中的位置——它在包被编译之前运行，通过 `println!("cargo:...")` 向 Cargo 回传指令，影响后续的编译与链接。
2. 解释 CUPTI 在经典 CUDA 安装中为什么位于 `<CUDA 根目录>/extras/CUPTI/` 而不是主 `include/`、`lib64/`，以及 `build.rs` 如何用 `is_dir()` 做「存在才追加」的增量处理。
3. 逐行看懂 `cc::Build` 的配置链（`cpp` / `std` / `warnings` / `file` / `includes` / `compile`），并说出 `cuda`、`cupti`、`stdc++` 三条链接指令各自的理由。
4. 掌握 `cargo:rerun-if-changed` 的精确语义：一旦发出该指令，Cargo 默认的「包内任意文件变化都重跑构建脚本」即被关闭。
5. 说清 CI 为什么把这个 crate 排除在 clippy 之外——本质是「构建期对 CUDA/CUPTI 的硬依赖」在无 GPU 环境上的必然代价。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 build.rs：Cargo 的构建脚本

`build.rs` 是 Cargo 约定的特殊文件：如果你的包根目录下有它，Cargo 会**先把它编译成可执行文件并运行**，然后才开始编译你的包。它通常用来：

- 生成 Rust 代码或头文件；
- 编译宿主机的 C/C++ 代码；
- 探测外部依赖（比如 CUDA 工具链）的位置。

构建脚本通过标准输出向 Cargo「回话」：所有以 `cargo:` 开头的行都是指令，其余行只是普通日志。本讲会见到三种指令：

| 指令 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `cargo:rustc-link-search=native=<路径>` | 告诉 rustc：链接时把这个路径加入库搜索路径（相当于给最终链接加一个 `-L`） |
| `cargo:rustc-link-lib=<名字>` | 告诉 rustc：最终链接时链接名为 `<名字>` 的库（相当于 `-l`） |
| `cargo:rerun-if-changed=<路径>` | 告诉 Cargo：只有这个路径变化时才重新运行构建脚本 |

一个关键心智模型：**这些指令不是立刻生效的**。它们被 Cargo 收集起来，在「最终把整个 crate（以及依赖它的二进制）链接成产物」的那一步才变成 `-L` / `-l` 参数。

### 2.2 编译与链接：两条搜索路径

C/C++ 构建要过两关，每关都有自己的搜索路径：

- **编译关（头文件）**：`#include <cupti.h>` 能否找到，取决于 `-I` 指定的头文件搜索路径（以及编译器的默认路径）。
- **链接关（库文件）**：`-lcupti` 要在 `-L` 指定的库搜索路径里找到 `libcupti.so` 或 `libcupti.a`（以及系统默认路径）。

pegainfer-cupti 的设计哲学是**错误前置**：CUDA/CUPTI 缺失时，让构建在编译期或链接期就失败，而不是把问题拖到运行期。三个阶段对应的失败形式：

| 阶段 | 缺什么 | 典型报错（示意） |
|---|---|---|
| 编译期 | 找不到 CUPTI 头文件 | `fatal error: cupti_profiler_target.h: No such file or directory` |
| 链接期 | 找不到 `libcupti` | `cannot find -lcupti` |
| 运行期 | （本项目设计上不允许漏到这里） | —— |

### 2.3 cc crate：build-dependency 里的常客

[cc](https://crates.io/crates/cc) 是 Rust 生态里最常用的构建依赖之一：它把「找到系统 C/C++ 编译器、拼参数、调用」包装成了声明式的 `cc::Build` API。本讲的 `build.rs` 用它把一份 C++ 源文件编成**静态库**。特别注意 `compile(name)` 这一步会自动做两件事：

1. 调用 C++ 编译器把所有 `.file(...)` 登记的源文件编成 `lib<name>.a`；
2. 自动向 Cargo 发出 `cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=<name>` 与指向产物目录的 `cargo:rustc-link-search` 指令。

也就是说，cc 负责「我自己编出来的库」的链接声明；**外部系统库**（CUDA、CUPTI、libstdc++）则要 build.rs 自己用 `cargo:rustc-link-lib` 声明——这是 4.3 节的主角。

### 2.4 CUPTI 是什么、装在哪

CUPTI（CUDA Profiling Tools Interface）是 NVIDIA 官方的性能分析接口层：读硬件性能计数器、做 kernel 时间线插桩都靠它。它与 nvcc、cuBLAS 这类「跑程序」的组件不同，属于「观测程序」的组件。因此在经典的 CUDA 安装中，它不在主 `include/`、`lib64/` 里，而在：

```
<CUDA 根目录>/extras/CUPTI/include   ← 头文件（如 cupti.h、cupti_profiler_target.h）
<CUDA 根目录>/extras/CUPTI/lib64     ← 库文件（libcupti.so）
```

`build.rs` 第 6 行的注释说的就是这件事，原文是：`// CUPTI ships outside the main toolkit dirs in classic installs.`（CUPTI 在经典安装中不随主工具链目录发布。）另外，各发行版也可能通过包管理器单独安装 CUPTI（装进系统头文件/库目录），所以探测逻辑必须容忍「extras 下没有」的情况——这正是 4.2 节 `is_dir()` 分支存在的原因。

### 2.5 workspace 依赖与本 crate 的「零运行时依赖」

看一眼 Cargo.toml 就能确认上一讲的结论：这个包**没有任何 `[dependencies]`**，只有 `[build-dependencies]`，且两条都是 `{ workspace = true }`——版本与配置由仓库根的 workspace 统一管理，本 crate 不自带版本号。`[lints] workspace = true` 表示它接受 workspace 统一的 lint 配置（这一点在 4.4 节还会用到）。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 角色 | 本讲怎么用它 |
|---|---|---|
| `pegainfer-cupti/build.rs` | 本讲主角：34 行构建脚本 | 全文逐行精读 |
| `pegainfer-cupti/Cargo.toml` | 包定义 | 只看 build-dependencies 与 lints 两节 |
| `pegainfer-cupti/csrc/range_profiler.cpp` | 被 build.rs 编译的 C++ 源文件 | 本讲只把它当「编译输入」；其内部实现留给单元 2 |
| `pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs` | `CudaToolkit` 探测 API 的定义处 | 通过 build.rs 的调用点反推其公开接口；定义行号本讲标注待确认 |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | CI 工作流 | 讨论对本 crate 的 clippy 排除；具体行号本讲标注待确认 |
| `pegainfer-cupti/src/lib.rs` | Rust 侧封装（下一站） | 本讲只在结尾指路，不深入 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

本讲的四个最小模块：

| 模块 | 解决的问题 |
|---|---|
| 4.1 CudaToolkit::discover 与 root/include_dirs | CUDA 装在哪？谁来统一回答？ |
| 4.2 CUPTI 头文件与 lib64 的 extras 路径处理 | CUPTI 藏在 extras，怎么找到又怎么容错？ |
| 4.3 cc 编译与链接指令输出 | C++ 源文件怎么变成静态库，链接清单怎么拼出来？ |
| 4.4 CI 排除该 crate 的原因 | 构建期硬依赖对 CI 意味着什么？ |

### 4.1 CudaToolkit::discover 与 root/include_dirs：先回答「CUDA 装在哪」

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

任何想引用 CUDA 头文件的原生代码构建，都要先回答同一个问题：**这台机器的 CUDA 工具链根目录在哪？** 答案并不唯一——可能是 `/usr/local/cuda` 软链接，可能是 `/usr/local/cuda-12.4`，可能是包管理器装的散件，也可能只存在于某个自定义前缀里；`nvcc` 可能在 `PATH` 里也可能不在。

openinfer workspace 的做法是把「找 CUDA」这件事抽成一个共享 crate：`pegainfer-build`，对外提供 `CudaToolkit` 类型。这样「CUDA 在哪」在整个仓库里只有一份答案，修一处、处处生效——这就是「单一事实来源」在构建系统里的体现（u1-l1 的实践已经让你用 `grep -rn "pegainfer-cupti" --include=Cargo.toml` 看过谁在引用谁；对 `pegainfer-build` 可以用同样的办法列出它的消费方）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

从 build.rs 的视角，探测与消费只有五步：

```
Cargo 启动 build.rs（注入 CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR 环境变量）
    │
    ▼
CudaToolkit::discover()            # 定位 CUDA 工具链，返回 toolkit
    │
    ├─ toolkit.root                # 工具链根目录（PathBuf），4.2 节用它拼 extras 路径
    ├─ toolkit.include_dirs        # 主工具链头文件目录集合 → 4.3 节喂给 cc
    └─ toolkit.link_search()       # 发出主工具链的 cargo:rustc-link-search 指令
```

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

build.rs 的开头 5 行（L4-L8）完成全部探测与路径准备：

> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L4-L8](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L4-L8)
> 这 5 行做了三件事：从 `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` 拿到包根目录、调用 `CudaToolkit::discover()` 探测工具链、再用 `toolkit.root` 拼出 CUPTI 的两个 extras 路径。

```rust
let manifest_dir = PathBuf::from(std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR").unwrap());
let toolkit = pegainfer_build::CudaToolkit::discover();
// CUPTI ships outside the main toolkit dirs in classic installs.
let cupti_include = toolkit.root.join("extras/CUPTI/include");
let cupti_lib64 = toolkit.root.join("extras/CUPTI/lib64");
```

三个细节：

- **L4 用 `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` 而不是相对路径**：Cargo 保证这个环境变量指向包根目录的绝对路径。build.rs 运行时的工作目录并不总是包根，用相对路径定位 `csrc/` 不可靠；L15 的 `.file(manifest_dir.join("csrc/range_profiler.cpp"))` 依赖这里的绝对化。
- **L5 是本 crate 与探测逻辑的唯一耦合点**：`discover()` 是无参关联函数，返回的 `toolkit` 随后在三处被消费——L7/L8 读 `.root`，L16 读 `.include_dirs`，L22 调 `.link_search()`。
- **L7/L8 的 `join` 只负责拼路径**，此刻没有任何 IO 发生；「这个路径存不存在」的判断留给 4.2 节的 `is_dir()`。

`toolkit` 的另外两个消费点：

> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L16](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L16)
> 把主工具链的头文件目录集合整体喂给 cc——这是 `-I` 参数的来源之一。

> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L22](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L22)
> 让探测逻辑自己发出主工具链的库搜索路径指令——这是 `-L` 参数的来源之一。

关于定义处 [pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-build/src/lib.rs)（内部行号**待确认**，本讲环境无法读取该文件），从上述调用点可以确证它的公开接口形状：

| 接口 | 从哪一行确证 | 推断的类型形状 |
|---|---|---|
| `CudaToolkit::discover()` | build.rs L5 | 关联函数，返回 `CudaToolkit` |
| `.root` | build.rs L7/L8 | `PathBuf`（能调 `join`） |
| `.include_dirs` | build.rs L16 | 能以 `&` 传入 `cc::Build::includes` 的目录集合（cc 要求 `IntoIterator<Item = AsRef<Path>>`，典型形状是 `Vec<PathBuf>`） |

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

```

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`CudaToolkit::discover()` 在 build.rs 里被调用了几次？它的结果被哪几行消费？

**答案**：`include_dirs` 直接服务 `-I`（L16，喂给 cc）；`root` 本身既不是 `-I` 也不是 `-L`，它是「拼出更多路径的原点」——本讲里它被用来拼 CUPTI 的 extras include 与 lib64 路径；主工具链的 `-L` 由 `link_search()`（L22）负责。

### 4.2 CUPTI 头文件与 lib64 的 extras 路径处理

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

经典安装的 CUDA 工具链目录大致长这样（**示意图**，具体条目随 CUDA 版本与安装形态变化）：

```
/usr/local/cuda/                 ← toolkit.root 指向这里
├── bin/                         ← nvcc 等
├── include/                     ← cuda.h、cublas_v2.h 等主头文件
├── lib64/                       ← 主库
└── extras/
    └── CUPTI/
        ├── include/             ← CUPTI 头文件
        └── lib64/               ← libcupti
```

CUPTI 被放在 `extras/` 下，是因为它**不参与程序的编译与运行**，只在「分析程序」时才需要——工具链把「跑起来必需」与「观测用」分开放。这带来一个构建上的麻烦：光知道 `toolkit.root` 还不够，还得知道 CUPTI 另有藏身处；而且**不是所有安装都有这个目录**（最小安装，或发行版把 CUPTI 单独装进系统目录的形态）。所以 build.rs 的策略是：extras 路径「**存在才追加，不存在就交给系统默认搜索路径**」。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```
cupti_include = root + "extras/CUPTI/include"
cupti_lib64   = root + "extras/CUPTI/lib64"

编译配置阶段：
    if cupti_include.is_dir()  → cc 追加这条 -I                    （L17-L19）
链接指令阶段：
    if cupti_lib64.is_dir()    → 发出 cargo:rustc-link-search=...   （L23-L25）

两个 if 都不命中（CUPTI 不在 extras）：
    → 不追加任何东西，编译器/链接器回落到系统默认搜索路径
    → 系统里装了 CUPTI（如包管理器形态）→ 一切正常
    → 系统里根本没有 CUPTI → 编译期（找不到头文件）或链接期（找不到库）失败
```

注意最后一点：**失败被明确地留在构建期**。这是有意设计——一个引用了 CUPTI 符号的二进制如果到运行时才发现缺库，排查成本高得多。

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

两个路径的定义已在 4.1.3 引用过（L7-L8）；这里看两处「条件追加」：

> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L17-L19](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L17-L19)
> 编译配置阶段：只有当 extras 下的 CUPTI include 目录真实存在时，才把它追加进 cc 的头文件搜索路径。

```rust

    build.include(&cupti_include);
}
```

> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L23-L25](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L23-L25)
> 链接指令阶段：同理，只有 extras 下的 CUPTI lib64 真实存在时，才向 Cargo 发出对应的库搜索路径指令。

    println!("cargo:rustc-link-search=native={}", cupti_lib64.display());

两个 if 语义完全对称：**一边管 `-I`，一边管 `-L`，都走「存在才追加」**。L22 的 `toolkit.link_search()` 先行发出主工具链的 `-L`，extras 这一条是叠加在它之后的增量。

### 4.3 cc 编译与链接指令输出：从一份 .cpp 到一张链接清单

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`cc::Build` 是「编译作业的声明式描述」：先链式登记属性，最后一次 `compile()` 收尾。收尾时它做两件事——把登记的源文件编成**静态库**，并自动发出链接这个静态库所需的 cargo 指令（见 2.3 节）。但 cc 只管「自己编的东西」；**外部系统库**（cuda、cupti、stdc++）必须由 build.rs 自己用 `cargo:rustc-link-lib` 一条条声明。本模块把这两段拼成一张完整的「链接清单」。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

build.rs 的 `main` 一共四段，一气呵成：

```
① 探测准备   L4-L8    manifest_dir、toolkit、两个 extras 路径（4.1/4.2 已讲）
② cc 编译    L10-L20  配置并编译 range_profiler.cpp → libpegainfer_cupti_range_profiler.a
③ 链接指令   L22-L31  主 -L、extras -L、三条 -l
④ 增量声明   L33      rerun-if-changed
```

最终 rustc 在链接时收到的库相关参数（**示意**，实际拼写以你机器上 `-v` 输出为准）：

```
-L <主工具链 lib64>                  ← toolkit.link_search()（L22）
-L <extras/CUPTI/lib64>              ← L24，存在时
-l pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler    ← cc 自动发出（静态库本体）
-l cuda                              ← L27
-l cupti                             ← L28
-l stdc++                            ← L30，非 Windows
```

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

cc 配置链：

> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L10-L20](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L10-L20)
> 用 cc 把 `csrc/range_profiler.cpp` 编成静态库：开 C++ 模式、锁 C++17、关警告、登记唯一的源文件、并入主工具链头文件路径，最后在 L20 收尾。

```rust
let mut build = cc::Build::new();
build
    .cpp(true)
    .std("c++17")
    .warnings(false)
    .file(manifest_dir.join("csrc/range_profiler.cpp"))
    .includes(&toolkit.include_dirs);
if cupti_include.is_dir() {
    build.include(&cupti_include);
}
build.compile("pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler");
```

逐项理由：

- `.cpp(true)`：使用 C++ 编译器驱动（g++/clang++），而非 C 编译器。
- `.std("c++17")`：实现代码按 C++17 编写，CUPTI 的 profiler 系列头文件与实现用到的语言特性以此为前提。
- `.warnings(false)`：相当于向编译器传 `-w`，屏蔽这份自带 C++ 文件的编译警告——它不参与日常 Rust lint 反馈环，警告只会制造噪音。
- `.file(...)`：只编译这一个文件——它就是上一讲认识的、约 400 行的 CUPTI 会话实现。
- `.includes(&toolkit.include_dirs)` 加上条件追加的 `.include(&cupti_include)`：头文件搜索路径的完整来源（主工具链 + 可能的 CUPTI extras）。
- `.compile("pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler")`：产出 `libpegainfer_cupti_range_profiler.a`，并自动发出 `cargo:rustc-link-lib=static=pegainfer_cupti_range_profiler` 与指向产物目录的 `rustc-link-search`。

链接指令段：

> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L27-L31](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L27-L31)
> 声明三个外部库：cuda（CUDA Driver API）、cupti（profiler API）、stdc++（C++ 标准库，Windows 除外）。

```rust
println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=cuda");
println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=cupti");
if !cfg!(target_os = "windows") {
    println!("cargo:rustc-link-lib=stdc++");
}
```

- `-lcuda`：实现在 C++ 里直接调用了 CUDA **Driver API**（如上下文获取与同步，详见单元 2/3 的讲义），这些符号在 `libcuda` 里。
- `-lcupti`：本 crate 的存在意义——`cuptiProfilerInitialize` 等一系列 profiler 符号都来自它。
- `-lstdc++`：C++ 实现用了标准库（异常、字符串等）；非 Windows 平台上最终链接由 rustc 驱动，不会自动带上 C++ 标准库，必须显式声明。Windows/MSVC 走另一套 CRT 链接机制，因此有 `if !cfg!(target_os = "windows")` 分支。

增量声明：

> [pegainfer-cupti/build.rs:L33](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/8886aa47b95bc4beedb63584eb367276650b2fec/pegainfer-cupti/build.rs#L33)
> 告诉 Cargo：只有这份 C++ 源文件变化时才重新运行构建脚本。

```rust
println!("cargo:rerun-if-changed=csrc/range_profiler.cpp");
```

语义要点（Cargo 手册规定）：

1. 如果一个 build.rs **没有**发出任何 `rerun-if-changed`，Cargo 采用保守策略——包内**任何**文件变化都重跑构建脚本。
2. 一旦发出了哪怕一条，保守策略即被关闭，Cargo 只监视列出的路径。
3. 构建脚本自身（`build.rs`）的变化永远会触发重跑，这是内建行为，不需要也不能用这条指令表达。

对这个 crate 而言，L33 意味着：改 `src/lib.rs`、改文档，都不会重跑 build.rs（自然也不会重编 C++）；只有改 `range_profiler.cpp`（或 `build.rs` 本身）才会。收益是构建更快；代价是：如果未来新增第二个 `.cpp`/`.cu` 文件却忘了同步登记 `rerun-if-changed`，改它不会触发重编——这是使用该指令时最常见的坑。
